summary: The article compares the NBA's Christmas Day games with the NFL's Thanksgiving Day games, weighing their histories, viewership and cultural significance. The NFL's Thanksgiving games draw far larger audiences, but the NBA's tradition is older and has global reach. It also notes the NFL's growing presence on Christmas Day as a potential threat to the NBA, and previews the 2023 NBA Christmas slate.
one_line: Essentially Sports compares NBA Christmas Day and NFL Thanksgiving Day games, finding the NFL ahead in viewership while the NBA tradition is older and global.
key_facts: The first NBA Christmas Day game dates back to 1947, when the league featured three games.
The NBA Christmas tradition is described as even older than the NFL's Super Bowl and is 77 years old.
Last season, NBA Christmas Day games averaged 4.27 viewers across all platforms, per the article.
NBA Christmas Day games attract about 200% more viewers than any other regular season game.
NFL Thanksgiving Day games this season averaged 34.1 million viewers across three games, surpassing last year's record of 33.6 million.
The combined unduplicated audience for the three NFL Thanksgiving games reached 133 million, the second-highest total on Thanksgiving, behind only last year.
Last year the NFL averaged 22.1 million viewers on its Christmas Day games.
The NFL's 2023 Christmas slate features Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Jalen Hurts.
Some estimates say the NFL's total Christmas viewership could outperform the NBA's by almost 75 million viewers.
NFL executives have said they won't schedule Christmas games if the holiday falls outside their regular broadcasting window.
NBA Christmas games are broadcast to over 200 countries and translated into more than 50 languages.
The 2023 NBA Christmas slate: Bucks vs Knicks at Madison Square Garden, Warriors vs Nuggets, Lakers vs Celtics, Heat vs Sixers, and Suns vs Mavs.
